baslik: Why the Tacoma Narrows Bridge Tore Itself Apart

sahneler.metin: This bridge tore itself apart in a forty mile an hour wind.
The deck twisted like a ribbon, then dropped into the water.
It had been open just four months.
So how did a steady wind destroy solid steel?
The wind made the deck flutter, and the flutter fed itself.
Each twist pumped in more energy than the bridge could shed.
One man escaped on his hands and knees.
Every long bridge since is tested in a wind tunnel.
